title: ר' פנחס בן יאיר

paragraphs: R' Pinhas ben Yair (in the Mishnah, Sotah 9:15). The author of Yuhasin did not include him in the ordered register of sages; in Ra'avad's Seder Ha-Kabbalah he wrote that he was Rabbi's colleague. In the chronological section under R' Shimon ben Yohai, Yuhasin writes: R' Pinhas ben Yair the pious, mentioned in the first chapter of Hullin 7a, who divided the river, etc. Rabbi went out to meet him and said, ‘Dine with me.’ He said yes, and Rabbi's face brightened (because Pinhas was not accustomed to benefiting from others, as Rashi explains); a mountain rose between them. This episode occurs differently in Jerusalem Talmud Ta’anit 3:1:3. Rabbi, R' Yishmael bar R' Yosi, and R' Elazar Ha-Kappar, with R' Pinhas ben Yair sitting before them (see there). In Jerusalem Talmud, Demai 1:3, and Bereshit Rabbah, Hayyei Sarah 60:8: robbers took his donkey, and it did not eat for three days. They pushed it outside lest it die and make the cave stink. When it came home, R' Pinhas ben Yair said, ‘It has not eaten for three days.’ They gave it food, but it would not eat. He said, ‘Perhaps the barley has not been duly tithed?’ His servants said that they had tithed it. He said, ‘Perhaps it is demai?’ Although one need not separate demai in this case, it had imposed a stricter rule upon itself. They separated demai and it ate. So too in Shekalim 5:1:7. In Jerusalem Talmud Demai 1:3:7–10, and Midrash Ekev, Devarim Rabbah 3:3: two poor men deposited two se'ah of barley with him. He sowed it and harvested it, and they needed to bring camels to take the barley away. There was a place where mice were eating the produce. They came to R' Pinhas ben Yair, who said, ‘Perhaps you have not duly tithed the produce?’ They tithed it, and the mice no longer ate it. A mouse swallowed the pearls of a king of Ishmael. He came to R' Pinhas ben Yair, who decreed that all the mice should assemble and disgorge the pearls; so it happened. He came to a place where they told him that the springs did not supply as much water as formerly. He said, ‘Perhaps you do not duly tithe the produce?’ They tithed it, and the supply was as before. All this is there; see there for many further deeds and miracles. In Shabbat 33b [Heilprin: 32b]: when R' Shimon ben Yohai and his son R' Elazar left the cave, R' Pinhas ben Yair, his son-in-law, heard and went out to meet him. Yuhasin writes [in the chronological section under R' Shimon ben Yohai] that the statement that he was his son-in-law appears to be a scribal error in the Gemara. In Zohar, Pinhas 84:532 [Heilprin: עתמ״ד], he appears to have been R' Shimon ben Yohai's father-in-law; Shalshelet Ha-Kabbalah likewise writes this. (In Zohar, Balak 24:293 [Heilprin: עש״ע]: R' Pinhas went to see his daughter, R' Elazar's mother. See Zohar, Shemini 2:10–13 [Heilprin: עמ״ב]: R' Pinhas ben Yair encountered R' Elazar. R' Elazar dismounted and kissed R' Pinhas ben Yair. R' Pinhas ben Yair opened, ‘May the Lord bless you,’ etc.; R' Elazar opened, ‘Children's children are the crown of elders,’ etc. From this midrash it appears that R' Elazar was R' Pinhas ben Yair's daughter's son. See there the episode of his donkey. Thus R' Shimon ben Yohai was R' Pinhas ben Yair's son-in-law. There is also some support in that R' Eliezer ben Yaakov, a pupil of R' Akiva, spoke in R' Pinhas ben Yair's name, while R' Shimon ben Yohai was also R' Akiva's pupil.) He lived long. When R' Shimon ben Yohai died, he saw R' Pinhas ben Yair and Rav Hamnuna the Elder, who had died earlier, coming to accompany him. (See Idra Zuta, Ha'azinu.) This is puzzling: since he died before R' Shimon ben Yohai—and R' Shimon ben Yohai died before his son R' Elazar, who died during Rabbi's lifetime, since Rabbi wished to marry his wife—how could R' Pinhas ben Yair have been in Rabbi's house? In the Tosefta, רבב״ג [Tosefta and Bavli: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] in the name of R' Yehudah ben Yair (see there); perhaps he was R' Pinhas ben Yair's brother. Here ends Yuhasin. In Jerusalem Talmud Ta’anit 3:4:5 [Heilprin: ע״ג, halakhah 4]: R' Berekhya, R' Abba bar Kahana, R' Yehoshua ben Yair in R' Pinhas ben Yair's name. R' Elazar ben Taddai was in his time. R' Eliezer ben Yaakov in his name. See Gilgulei Neshamot §116: R' Pinhas ben Yair, Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai, and our holy Rabbi are one spark (this needs examination: since he was in Rabbi's generation as above, how were they one spark?). In Asarah Ma'amarot [בפ״י י״מ; location unresolved]: R' Pinhas ben Yair is a spark of Avraham, and his stolen donkey was to rectify the soul of Ishmael, among whom there are thieves. See Yalkut Reuveni, Balak, folio 154, column 3, citing ע״ה ד״ח [abbreviations unresolved]. Ishmael, together with its six letters, has the numerical value of aton, ‘she-ass’ (ג״נ; same provisional title). The evil in Esav was reincarnated in R' Pinhas ben Yair's donkey (עב״א תפ״ח; citation unresolved). In Avodah Zarah 20b, R' Pinhas ben Yair holds that piety is greater than all the other qualities, because he is at the level of hesed, as found in Zohar, Aharei [עקי״א]. See Bereshit [על״ח]: Avraham's level; through Avraham's merit he divided the river three times. ‘Ginnai nahara,’ with one additional unit, has the numerical value of eshel (Asarah Ma'amarot, Ma'amar Hakor Din, Part IV, chapter 14). He composed Midrash Tadshe: its numerical value is ‘zeh Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair’ (Zikkukin De-Nura, beginning of the book). It seems to me that one should write פינחס, with a yod, or ‘zehu de-Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair.’ His burial is in Kefar Bar'am (גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]).
